title: Fixed-residue small lifts give sections of truncated extensions
statement:
Let $R,A$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $A$, let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be a prime ideal, and put $S=A_{\mathfrak q}$ and $k=S/\mathfrak qS$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $C$ be a Noetherian local commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with a surjective $R$-algebra map $p:C\twoheadrightarrow S$. Write $J=\ker p$ and $\mathfrak m$ for the unique maximal ideal of $C$. Suppose the following fixed-residue lifting property holds. For every surjection $\varphi:B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ of nonzero Artinian local commutative rings, with $\operatorname{length}_{B'}\ker\varphi=1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length], and specified isomorphisms $B'/\mathfrak m_{B'}\cong k$ and $B/\mathfrak m_B\cong k$ under which the residue map of $\varphi$ is the identity, every pair of ring maps $\rho:R\to B'$ and $a:A\to B$ satisfying $a\circ(R\to A)=\varphi\circ\rho$ and whose composite $A\to B\to k$ is the canonical map $A\to S\to k$ admits $a':A\to B'$ with $\varphi a'=a$ and $a'\circ(R\to A)=\rho$. Here Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize, and local means there is a unique maximal ideal. Then for every integer $N\ge1$ the canonical quotient map of $R$-algebras
$$C/(J^2+\mathfrak m^N)\longrightarrow C/(J+\mathfrak m^N)$$
has an $R$-algebra section.

source.place: Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1), paragraphs beginning Let N and Applying condition (4); fixed-residue refinement of the truncated-section construction.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qS$, $I=J^2+\mathfrak m^N$, $L=J+\mathfrak m^N$, $E=C/I$ and $F=C/L$. Since $p$ is surjective, $p^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ is maximal, hence equals $\mathfrak m$; consequently $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and $p(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak n$. Thus $\mathfrak m^N\subseteq I\subseteq L\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] to both defining ideals: $E,F$ are nonzero Artinian local rings with maximal ideals the images of $\mathfrak m$, and these maximal ideals have $N$th power zero. Quotient representatives identify $F=S/\mathfrak n^N$: the kernel of $C\to S/\mathfrak n^N$ is $J+\mathfrak m^N$, since $p(\mathfrak m^N)=\mathfrak n^N$. Denote the induced surjections by $\pi:E\to F$ and $t:S\to F$. Reduction of either quotient modulo its maximal ideal identifies its residue field with $C/\mathfrak m=S/\mathfrak n=k$; the residue map of $\pi$ is the identity.

source.place: Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1), paragraphs beginning Let N and Applying condition (4)

proof.text: Let $K=\ker\pi$, the image of $J$ in $E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ideal-length-one-filtration] to obtain ideals $0=K_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_r=K$ with $K_{i+1}/K_i$ of $E$-module length one. Put $D_i=E/K_i$ and use the canonical identification $D_r=F$, $D_0=E$. Every $K_i$ lies in the maximal ideal of $E$. Its inverse image $H_i\subset C$ therefore satisfies $\mathfrak m^N\subseteq H_i\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The quotient lemma [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local], applied to $H_i$, shows that $D_i=C/H_i$ is nonzero Artinian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/H_i$. Specify its residue identification $D_i/(\mathfrak m/H_i)=C/\mathfrak m=k$. Each quotient map $\delta_i:D_i\twoheadrightarrow D_{i+1}$ induces the identity on these specified residue fields.

source.place: Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1), paragraphs beginning Let N and Applying condition (4)

proof.text: The kernel of $\delta_i$ is $K_{i+1}/K_i$: an element of $E/K_i$ maps to zero precisely when its representative belongs to $K_{i+1}$. Its submodules for the $E$-action and the $D_i$-action are identical, since $E\twoheadrightarrow D_i$ is surjective and the action factors through it. Hence its $D_i$-module length is also one, directly from the chain definition [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Write $\rho_i:R\to D_i$ for the structural map and $\pi_i:D_i\to F$ for the quotient. Starting with $a_r:A\to S\xrightarrow{t}F=D_r$, induct downwards to maps $a_i:A\to D_i$ satisfying $\pi_i a_i=a_r$, $a_i\circ(R\to A)=\rho_i$, and residue composite the canonical $A\to k$. At a downward step apply the assumed fixed-residue lifting property to $\delta_i$, $\rho_i$, and $a_{i+1}$; its compatibility equation is $a_{i+1}\circ(R\to A)=\delta_i\rho_i$. The returned lift has the required residue composite because $\delta_i$ is the identity on residues. Composition with $\pi_{i+1}$ preserves the other invariant. Thus $a'=a_0:A\to E$ satisfies $\pi a'=t\circ(A\to S)$ and is $R$-compatible. If $r=0$, the starting map already gives $a'$.

source.place: Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1), paragraphs beginning Let N and Applying condition (4)

proof.text: The residue composite of $a'$ is $A\to k$, whose kernel is $\mathfrak q$. For $s\notin\mathfrak q$, $a'(s)$ therefore lies outside the maximal ideal of $E$ and is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion]. Define $b:S\to E$ on fractions [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] by $b(x/s)=a'(x)a'(s)^{-1}$. If $u(xs'-x's)=0$ with $u\notin\mathfrak q$, applying $a'$ and cancelling the unit $a'(u)$ proves that this formula is independent of representatives. Addition and multiplication of fractions prove it is a ring map. It is $R$-compatible since its value on $r/1$ is $\rho_0(r)$. Moreover $\pi b=t$: the two maps agree on $A$, and on every $x/s$ both take the value $t(x)t(s)^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1), paragraphs beginning Let N and Applying condition (4)

proof.text: If $x/s\in\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qS$, then $x\in\mathfrak q$, so $a'(x)$ has zero residue in $k$. Thus $b(\mathfrak n)$ is contained in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_E$ of $E$. This ideal has $N$th power zero by Step 1; products of $N$ such images vanish, whence $b(\mathfrak n^N)=0$. The formula $\sigma(y+\mathfrak n^N)=b(y)$ consequently defines an $R$-algebra map $\sigma:F=S/\mathfrak n^N\to E$. For every $y\in S$, $\pi\sigma(t(y))=\pi b(y)=t(y)$ by Step 4. As $t$ is surjective, $\pi\sigma=\mathrm{id}_F$. Under the quotient identifications of Step 1 this is the required section $C/(J+\mathfrak m^N)\to C/(J^2+\mathfrak m^N)$. For $N=1$ both quotients equal $C/\mathfrak m$, and for $J=0$ the quotient map itself is the identity.

Step 4: units come from ker(A->k)=q, and the fraction map is well defined, R-compatible, and satisfies pi b = t. Step 5: b(n) lies in m_E and m_E^N = 0, so b descends to a section. Edge cases checked: N=1, J=0, r=0, C a field. lean.statement: theorem fixed_residue_lifts_truncated_section {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {C : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R C] (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime] [IsNoetherianRing C] [IsLocalRing C] (p : C →ₐ[R] Localization.AtPrime q) (hp : Function.Surjective p) (hlift : ∀ (B' B : Type (max u v w t)) [CommRing B'] [CommRing B] [IsArtinianRing B'] [IsArtinianRing B] [IsLocalRing B'] [IsLocalRing B] (φ : B' →+* B), Function.Surjective φ → Module.length B' (RingHom.ker φ) = 1 → ∀ (e' : IsLocalRing.ResidueField B' ≃+* q.ResidueField) (e : IsLocalRing.ResidueField B ≃+* q.ResidueField), e'.toRingHom.comp (IsLocalRing.residue B') = (e.toRingHom.comp (IsLocalRing.residue B)).comp φ → ∀ (ρ : R →+* B') (a : A →+* B), a.comp (algebraMap R A) = φ.comp ρ → (e.toRingHom.comp (IsLocalRing.residue B)).comp a = algebraMap A q.ResidueField → ∃ a' : A →+* B', φ.comp a' = a ∧ a'.comp (algebraMap R A) = ρ) : ∀ (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → ∃ σ : (C ⧸ (RingHom.ker p.toRingHom ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C ^ N)) →ₐ[R] (C ⧸ (RingHom.ker p.toRingHom ^ 2 ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C ^ N)), (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ R (sup_le_sup (Ideal.pow_le_self (by decide : 2 ≠ 0)) le_rfl)).comp σ = AlgHom.id R _
